judgements.reason: DenseGraphLimits still needs a stacked analytic chain: mod-null realignment and martingale compactness of GraphonSpaceI feed the convergence equivalence, graphon-mixture existence and uniqueness, and then Lovasz-Szegedy representability, alongside the sampling lemmas behind inverse counting. SchurWeyl's remaining Murnaghan-Nakayama, Frobenius characteristic with Jacobi-Trudi, RSK, Schur-functor decomposition and Brauer-algebra O/Sp duality with its semisimplicity are comparable in bulk but mostly parallel lanes on an already built Specht, double-centralizer, Weyl-module and Brauer-diagram base.

EllipticCurves lacks the dual isogeny and degree form, Weil pairing and Tate module, Hasse bound, reduction theory with Neron-Ogg-Shafarevich, Tate's algorithm and the Tate curve, global minimal models, and the Galois-cohomological Selmer/Sha layer. DenseGraphLimits lacks only compactness, inverse counting, the mixture and representability theorems and sampling convergence on a largely built graphon library.

EllipticCurves has more unbuilt graduate theory across many lanes: dual isogeny, Weil pairing and Tate module, Hasse and zeta, the reduction filtration and Neron-Ogg-Shafarevich, Tate's algorithm and curve, global minimal models, and Selmer/Sha with Galois-cohomology packaging and Cassels. FuchsianOrbifolds needs complex structures on quotients, the Poincare polygon theorem, cusp compactification and a Riemann-surface degree theory whose Riemann-Hurwitz imports an unbuilt CW Euler characteristic and surface triangulation; that is deep but smaller in total.

CombinatorialHeegaardFloer still needs grid-homology invariance (pentagon/hexagon maps, stabilization cones), the F[U] structure theorem, tau with the Milnor conjecture and slice-genus bound, sign assignments and the filtered theory, lattice homology with Neumann invariance, stable HF-hat of 3-manifolds and the Cromwell/Reidemeister reconciliation. FuchsianOrbifolds needs quotient complex structures, the polygon theorem, compactification and a degree theory resting on imported CW Euler characteristics, j and P^1: deep, but less theory overall.

ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology needs Huber's etale cohomology of adic spaces (formal models, nearby cycles over valuation rings, duality for curves, comparison and compactification) on top of imported and unbuilt SGA4 etale cohomology, EDC duality, perfectoid spaces and prismatic inputs. CombinatorialHeegaardFloer's remaining grid, lattice and stable-HF-hat combinatorics sits on Mathlib homological algebra, with d^2 = 0 already proved.

EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves imports every ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology layer through its EDC.6 comparison, and adds diamond etale cohomology with the six operations, Weil I/II with hard Lefschetz, perverse sheaves and the decomposition theorem. ClassicalAdic's own imports reach only EDC.0-4, so the theory it needs is a strict part of the other's.

Both need SGA4 etale cohomology, EDC.0-5 duality and perverse sheaves and Weil II. GlobalShtukas then adds algebraic stacks, Bruhat-Tits parahorics, function-field automorphic forms, and its Satake/shtuka/Drinfeld-lemma/excursion stack with L. Lafforgue's GL_n; EtaleDuality adds, through EDC.6 (on which its decomposition theorem EDC.7 builds), Huber's adic etale cohomology, perfectoid spaces, diamonds and ECD's six operations with alterations and prismatic inputs, plus mixed complexes and hard Lefschetz, which is comparable in bulk and stacked slightly deeper.

HeegnerPointEulerSystems needs modularity of elliptic curves (Khare-Wintenberger with modularity lifting), Shimura curves and CM theory, Gross-Zagier heights, Euler and Kolyvagin systems and anticyclotomic main conjectures, and its imports already contain most of GlobalShtukas's etale-cohomological base. GlobalShtukas adds only its own Satake/shtuka/Lafforgue stack with stack, parahoric and function-field inputs.

HeegnerPointEulerSystems stacks CM points, Kolyvagin descent and main conjectures on elliptic-curve modularity, Shimura varieties, Gross-Zagier, p-adic Hodge theory and the full etale-cohomology stack, none of it built. HeegaardFloer's analytic Floer tower (Morse homology, the elliptic Cauchy-Riemann package, Gromov compactness and gluing, HF-hat in Sym^g) builds on Mathlib analysis, with Sard-Smale and Fredholm level sets already in Tau Ceti.

AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII needs unitary Shimura varieties with compactifications, the stabilized trace formula with the fundamental lemma, local Langlands for GL_n, Igusa varieties, eigenvarieties and p-adic Hodge theory, on top of all of etale duality, Weil II and the diamond machinery. HeegaardFloer's missing analytic tower (elliptic estimates, J-holomorphic compactness and gluing, Lagrangian and Heegaard Floer homology) is large but rests on existing Mathlib and Tau Ceti analysis.

ClassicalSerreModularity imports all of GL2ModularityLifting (patching, Pan's theorem, completed cohomology, p-adic local Langlands for GL2(Q_p)), potential modularity, Serre weights, GL2 transfer, modular curves, Neron models and Faltings finiteness, and its imports already include the fundamental lemma, local Langlands for GL_n and AG2.0-AG2.1a. AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII adds only its own Shin, Chenevier-Harris and HLTT constructions with the Igusa and unitary trace-comparison stages.

ClassicalSerreModularity imports every GL2ModularityLifting layer (R22 patching and R32 de Rham lifting) and additionally needs potential modularity and compatible systems, Fontaine/Schoof base cases with Faltings and Arakelov inputs, and the Khare-Wintenberger induction. The theory GL2ModularityLifting needs is a strict part of it.

GL2ModularityLifting's imports contain RelativeFarguesFontaine's curve, divisor and patching layers (through p-adic Hodge and A_inf inputs) together with deformation rings, patching, Shimura-curve Hecke modules, completed cohomology and p-adic local Langlands for GL2(Q_p). RelativeFarguesFontaine needs only the relative curve, its line bundles and Beauville-Laszlo gluing over perfectoid spaces, diamonds and the absolute-curve comparisons.

EllipticCurves still lacks the dual isogeny, Weil pairing, Tate module, Hasse bound, reduction theory, Tate's algorithm and curve, global minimal models, and Selmer/Sha with its Galois cohomology. SchurWeyl lacks only Murnaghan-Nakayama, the Frobenius characteristic and RSK, Schur-functor decomposition and Brauer-algebra O/Sp duality on a largely built base.

Beyond the perfectoid spaces and diamonds both need, EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves requires SGA4 etale cohomology, Verdier and Poincare duality, cycle classes, perverse sheaves, Weil I/II, Huber's adic etale cohomology and the ECD six operations. RelativeFarguesFontaine adds only analytification and sousperfectoid adic geometry, the absolute-curve diamond comparisons, and its relative curve, divisors, B_dR and Beauville-Laszlo gluing.

ClassicalSerreModularity's imports contain every ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology layer (through etale duality and p-adic Hodge inputs) plus modularity lifting, potential modularity, Serre weights, GL2 transfer and completed cohomology. ClassicalAdic needs only Huber's adic etale cohomology with its SGA4, perfectoid and duality imports.

FuchsianOrbifolds needs complex structures on elliptic quotients, the Poincare polygon theorem and triangle groups, horodisc compactification, and a compact-Riemann-surface degree theory with Riemann-Hurwitz resting on unbuilt CW Euler characteristics, j and P^1. DenseGraphLimits needs a handful of analytic theorems (compactness, inverse counting, mixtures, representability, sampling convergence) on a mostly built graphon library.

AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII's imports contain RelativeFarguesFontaine's curve, divisor and patching layers along with the whole etale-duality, Weil II and diamond stack, Shimura varieties, the fundamental lemma, local Langlands for GL_n and eigenvarieties. RelativeFarguesFontaine needs only perfectoid and diamond foundations and its relative curve construction.

HeegnerPointEulerSystems imports GL2 modularity lifting (R22) inside elliptic-curve modularity via Khare-Wintenberger, plus potential modularity, Gross-Zagier, Euler and Kato systems, K-theory and main conjectures. GL2ModularityLifting's extra pieces (R32 de Rham lifting, completed cohomology, p-adic local Langlands for GL2(Q_p)) are far smaller.

GlobalShtukas needs SGA4 etale cohomology, duality, perverse sheaves, Weil I/II and algebraic stacks, none of which the libraries have, before geometric Satake, shtuka cohomology, Drinfeld's lemma and L. Lafforgue's GL_n. HeegaardFloer's missing Morse homology, elliptic Cauchy-Riemann theory, Gromov compactness and gluing, HF-hat with its flavours, bordered/cylindrical theory and the reconciliations (which consume the unbuilt combinatorial lanes) is nearly as large, but it is stacked less deeply and builds on Mathlib analysis and Tau Ceti's Fredholm and Sard-Smale work.

CombinatorialHeegaardFloer still needs grid-homology invariance, tau and the Milnor conjecture, slice-genus and Legendrian results, lattice-homology invariance, stable HF-hat of 3-manifolds and the knot-theory reconciliation. SchurWeyl lacks only Murnaghan-Nakayama, the Frobenius characteristic and RSK, Schur-functor decomposition and Brauer-algebra O/Sp duality over a largely built base.

AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII imports every EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves layer (perverse sheaves, the decomposition theorem, the comparisons) and adds Shimura varieties with compactifications, the stabilized trace formula and fundamental lemma, local Langlands for GL_n, Igusa varieties, eigenvarieties and its own Galois constructions.

HeegnerPointEulerSystems's imports contain all of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology together with elliptic-curve modularity, Shimura curves, Gross-Zagier, Euler systems and Iwasawa main conjectures. ClassicalAdic needs only Huber's adic etale cohomology with its SGA4, duality and perfectoid imports.

FuchsianOrbifolds needs Riemann-surface charts on quotients, the Poincare polygon theorem, cusp compactification, and degree theory with Riemann-Hurwitz that imports unbuilt CW Euler characteristics, j and P^1. SchurWeyl's remaining Murnaghan-Nakayama, Frobenius characteristic and RSK, Schur-functor decomposition and Brauer O/Sp duality sit on a largely built Specht and double-centralizer base.
